subject: Q3 cross-team sync: action cadence & exec asks

From: Evan Myers <evan@datacloud.com>

Cc: procurement@datacloud.com
Date: 2026-08-17T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Q3 alignment & QBR prep — proposed MAP and ask list

Hi Aisha / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — team was impressed with the latencies you quoted. We agreed internally to surface a short mutual action plan ahead of our QBR on Sept 8. To keep the week-of prep lightweight, could you confirm the following by end-of-day Tuesday?

- Flag any hard-blocks on the Dedicated capacity timeline (we need guarantee by Aug 31).
- Provide a short list of exec asks/SLAs we should expect in the QBR (2–3 items).
- Share the compatibility checklist (data retention + audit log) that procurement asked for.

I attached a skeleton MAP that our PM drafted — feel free to overwrite.

Best,
Evan

Attachment: QBR-MAP-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-08-17T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q3 alignment & QBR prep — proposed MAP and ask list

Thanks Evan — looping in Marissa and Vivek for the delivery and SLA items. Quick answers inline: 

- Dedicated capacity timeline: we can commit to production-ready pool available by Aug 31 for the "standard" profile (8x A100 equivalent). Any additional capacity beyond that (burst / custom isolation) is likely Sept 14. We will put a firm SLA exception request if DataCloud needs the latter earlier.
- Exec asks we plan to present (draft): 1) SLA: 99.9% uptime with P99 latency targets per route; 2) Data residency & audit log cadence; 3) Cost predictability plan (commit tiers + overage controls).
- Compatibility checklist: attached PDF (procurement-friendly).

I'll make these explicit on the MAP and drop a short slide for the QBR. Marissa — can you own the SLA language and Vivek, can you confirm the timeline + exception ask wording?

Thanks,
Aisha

> I'll make these explicit on the MAP and drop a short slide for the QBR. Marissa — can you own the SLA language and Vivek, can you confirm the timeline + exception ask wording?

Yep, I'll take SLA language. Draft below (feel free to edit):

- Proposed SLA ask (for QBR): 99.9% availability, P95 < 120ms, P99 < 450ms for standard routes; escalation playbook + credit schedule for sustained breaches.
- Exception path: if DataCloud requires guaranteed burst capacity above 2x, we propose a defined reservation fee + 4-week lead time.

Action items for this thread: 
1) Marissa: finalize SLA text and credits (owner) — due 2026-08-19 EOD.
2) Vivek: confirm Dedicated pool readiness by Aug 31 and scope of exception (owner) — due 2026-08-18 morning.
3) Aisha: send QBR slide & MAP update to Evan by Aug 19 midday.

I'll also add a short appendix enumerating recovery & fallback policies for the QBR slide.

—Marissa
Head of Customer Success

Quick update: infra has validated the standard profile pool (8x A100 equiv) and scheduler tests pass at expected throughput. We're green for Aug 31 delivery for that profile. 

Exception ask details: for guaranteed burst >2x, we'll need a reservation commit and a 14–28 day pre-warm window depending on region. If DataCloud needs this in US-West specifically, we can target a 14-day lead time with a 15% premium on reserved hours.

I've attached a short runbook excerpt to call out operational handoffs during bursts.

Vivek
